question: To complete a wall, Vijay takes 40 percent more time than Ramesh. If together they complete the wall in 25 days, then how much time will Vijay alone take to complete it?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time Ratio (Vijay : Ramesh) = 140 : 100 = 7 : 5

Efficiency Ratio (Vijay : Ramesh) = 5 : 7 (Inversely proportional to time)

Combined Efficiency = 5 + 7 = 12 units/day

Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Together Time = 12 × 25 = 300 units

Vijay's alone time = Total Work ÷ Vijay's Efficiency = 300 ÷ 5 = 60 days

**∴ The correct answer is 60 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Vijay and Ramesh together = 25 days

Vijay's time = Ramesh's time + 40% of Ramesh's time

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Combined Time

Combined efficiency of Vijay + Ramesh = 5 + 7 = 12 units/day

⇒ Let Ramesh's time be TR and Vijay's time be TV

⇒ TV = 1.4 × TR ⇒ TV/TR = 14/10 = 7/5

⇒ 1/TV + 1/TR = 1/25

⇒ 1/TV + 1.4/TV = 1/25

⇒ 2.4 / TV = 1/25

⇒ TV = 25 × 2.4 = 60 days

**∴ The correct answer is 60 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of time is a:b, then the ratio of efficiency is b:a.

Total Work Formula

Total Work = Individual Efficiency × Individual Time or Combined Efficiency × Combined Time.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the work done, which is equivalent to the ratio of efficiencies when everyone works for the same duration.</p
